resources.string: Double-tap anywhere to capture your screen
Shake your phone to capture your screen
Volume Down then Up to capture your screen
Tap the floating button to capture your screen
Double-Tap — tap twice quickly in the trigger zone
Shake — shake your phone to capture
Volume Keys — press Volume Down then Volume Up
Accessibility Button — tap the floating system button
Best option: your phone\'s built-in gesture

Pixel phones can take a screenshot when you double-tap the BACK of the phone. It cannot be triggered by swiping or tapping the screen, so it never fires by accident.\n\nSettings → System → Gestures → Quick Tap → Take screenshot
Turn this on in Settings → Accessibility → DoubleTap Screenshot → Shortcut, then tap the floating button to capture.
Permission to read photos is required to list your screenshots. Grant it in Settings → Apps → DoubleTap Screenshot → Permissions.
An error was recorded — copy this and send it
Crash details copied — paste them to report the problem
Taps only count inside this area. Restricting the zone is the only reliable way to stop apps\' own double-tap gestures (zoom, like, select text) from firing screenshots.
Screen corners — recommended, almost no app uses them
Top of screen — the status bar strip
Bottom of screen — below the content area
Anywhere — expect false triggers in many apps
Pause capture while you type. Detects the keyboard window, a focused text field, and recent typing, so it works even with keyboards that hide themselves from the system.
Fast — requires quick taps (less false triggers)
Relaxed — more time between taps (easier to trigger)
Triple-Tap — three taps to capture (fewer false triggers)

To get started:

1. Tap the button above
2. Find "DoubleTap Screenshot" in the list
3. Toggle it ON and confirm

Once enabled, double-tap anywhere on your screen to take a screenshot. Nothing visible is added to your screen.

Double-tap inside your Trigger Zone to take a screenshot.
Four taps start/stop screen recording.

A short vibration confirms the capture. There is a 2-second cooldown between screenshots.

If screenshots fire by accident, set the Trigger Zone to Screen Corners below.
Shake your phone to take a screenshot.\n\nA short vibration confirms the capture. There is a 2-second cooldown between screenshots.
Press Volume Down then Volume Up quickly to take a screenshot.\n\nThe two presses cancel out, so your volume stays where it was. This trigger never fires by accident from tapping.

Tap the floating accessibility button to take a screenshot.\n\nIf you do not see it, enable it in Settings → Accessibility → DoubleTap Screenshot → Shortcut. Android draws and positions the button, so swipes and taps never trigger it by accident.
Detection is paused. Tap Resume to start capturing screenshots again.

Triple-tap inside your Trigger Zone to take a screenshot.
Five taps start/stop screen recording.

A short vibration confirms the capture. Three taps reduces false triggers further.
Name screenshots with date, app name, and location
Location permission needed for auto-naming with location
Show share popup after taking a screenshot
Draw rectangles over areas to blur
Detects double-tap gestures or shake anywhere on screen and takes a screenshot. Nothing visible is added to your screen. The service does not collect or transmit any data.
Automatically add watermark text to screenshots
Tap the lines you want, then Copy.
Text extraction unavailable — the text model may still be downloading. Try again in a moment.
Record your screen — tap to start, notification to stop

Capture sound from the microphone while recording. Android does not let an app record the audio playing inside other apps, so game and video sound is only picked up through the mic when the speaker is on.
Microphone permission is needed to record audio
